Chapter 11: The Practice of Letting Go
Letting go—it's easily one of the hardest things we ever have to do, isn't it? And yet, more often than not, it’s the key to actually moving forward. Most of us hold on so tightly—to old stories, past hurts, maybe even dreams that just don’t fit anymore. That grip can feel safe at first, almost protective. But over time, it starts to weigh us down.
If you’ve ever learned to let go, even just a little, you probably know the kind of freedom it brings. Suddenly, there’s room to breathe.
Think about the story of someone who held onto resentment for years. A friendship ended badly, and the hurt just lingered. Every time that memory popped up, so did the anger. But then—by total chance—the two crossed paths again. There was an awkward conversation, some honest apologies, and a big decision to finally move on. The pain didn’t magically disappear, but that heavy weight? It lifted. Life suddenly felt lighter, more open.
Most of us don’t realize just how much energy we spend holding on. Maybe it’s not forgiving yourself for a mistake. Or maybe it’s a parent clinging to how things “should” be. Sometimes it’s about resenting a missed opportunity at work. All these things—we carry them like invisible backpacks.
But here’s the thing: letting go doesn’t mean you’re forgetting, or pretending those things didn’t matter. It’s more about making some space for what’s next.
There’s another story, too—a person who had to let go of a dream. Years of hard work had gone into building a career, but then life changed. At first, there was grief—a real sense of loss. But, over time, new doors started to open. A different path appeared, one that hadn’t even been considered before. What felt like an ending at first actually became a turning point.
So, letting go isn’t just a single moment—it’s a practice. It’s about noticing what you’re holding onto, and slowly, gently, loosening that grip. Most of us don’t really notice how much lighter life can be, until we make a little room for what’s possible.
